title: deprecate-monolithic-lint-runner-adopt-plugin-adapter
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce plugin adapter for lint/test pipelines. No breaking runtime changes; repository owners must update .lint-plugins manifest. Rolling migration recommended.
description: Motivation: our monolithic lint runner (tools/monolith-lint/) has become a maintenance bottleneck: adding new linters or adjusting staging semantics required touching a large Golang binary and CI glue. This PR replaces the monolith with a small, stable adapter and a plugin interface and migrates existing linters to the new plugin contract. Goals: 1) reduce CI startup surface, 2) enable per-repo plugin bundles, 3) allow non-Go linters to run as thin adapters (Python/JS), 4) simplify release automation by decoupling lint plugin lifecycle from the main runtime. Summary of changes: - Add docs/ci/lint-plugin-spec.md describing the plugin contract (manifest format, env, exit codes, caching hints). - Introduce tools/lint-adapter/ (minimal Go shim) that discovers plugins via repository .lint-plugins and executes them with sandboxed env. - Convert existing internal linters to plugin wrappers under tools/plugins/{golang-lint,rust-lint,js-lint}. These are thin shims that call existing linters but conform to the adapter API. - Update .github/workflows/lint.yml to call the adapter and add a staged fast-path for changed files only. - Add a migration script scripts/migrate-lint-manifest.py that translates old repo-level lint config to the new .lint-plugins manifest. - Update release automation hooks to include plugin-version checks in the release-smoke job (prevents shipping without compatible plugin manifests). Migration notes: - Repositories should add .lint-plugins at root. The PR includes migration script output for our monorepo root and the most common subpackages (examples/, sdk/). - For external repos, admins can opt-in by adding the manifest or continue using the legacy runner for 2 release cycles (legacy runner kept under tools/monolith-lint/compat/). Rollout plan: - Phase 1 (this PR): land adapter + plugin wrappers in monorepo; update monorepo CI to use adapter. - Phase 2: run repo-level migration across 50 high-activity repos using the migration script and the automation bot (Linear ENG-1982). - Phase 3: deprecate legacy runner and remove compat directory after 2 release cycles. Checklist: - [x] Spec for plugin contract - [x] Adapter implementation - [x] Existing linters migrated to plugin wrappers - [x] CI workflow updated with fast-path changed-files optimization - [x] Migration script added - [x] Release-smoke checks updated - [x] Documentation: docs/ci/lint-plugin-spec.md Tests and CI: initial run showed integration failures due to PATH differences in GitHub Actions; fixed by normalizing PATH in adapter and adding explicit tool cache restoration. Final CI matrix: unit-tests (pass), lint (pass via adapter), integration (pass), release-smoke (pass), dependency-bot (pass). Rollback plan: re-enable tools/monolith-lint/compat/entrypoint in the lint workflow and revert head_branch; compat entrypoint retained for two cycles. Related: ENG-2110 (release automation: validate plugin versions), RFC-2025 (lint plugin contract). Detailed rationale: consolidating the runner surface but modularizing plugins gives us improved iteration velocity (add a new linter by shipping a small plugin), better test isolation, and smaller hotfix blast radius for emergency lint fixes. The adapter is intentionally small and covered by unit tests and a lightweight integration test that runs in CI smoke.

review_comments: Evan Liu: Nice decomposition. Two asks: 1) add a strict schema for .lint-plugins so the adapter can validate early; 2) ensure plugin stderr scanning doesn't leak secrets.

Maya Patel (author): added docs/ci/lint-plugin-spec.md with JSON schema and implemented early validation in adapter. stderr now filtered by default; plugin authors can opt-in with an allowlist in the manifest.
Sofia Ramirez: CI speed looks good for changed-files path. Can we add a soft-fail flag for flaky third-party linters so repo owners can triage?
Maya Patel: added plugin manifest field 'soft_fail' and the adapter supports it; added notes in docs and tests.
